REAL ESTATE TAXES MUST BE PAID OR POSTMARKED BY SEPTEMBER 18, 2026
CHANGES IN STATE LAW RESULT IN LATER PROPERTY TAX DEADLINE FOR 2nd HALF PAYMENT
Implementation of the changes resulting from the passage of House Bill 186 has caused delays in issuing tax bills and establishing due dates across the state. “When this legislation was under consideration, County Treasurer’s across Ohio warned the General Assembly that tax bill delays would be a likely result,” said Mahoning County Treasurer Dan Yemma. “This has proven to be the case.”
HB186 created an Inflation Cap Credit for qualifying property classifications. “The amount of the credit will vary for properties that qualify,” adds Treasurer Yemma. “Taxes will remain more or less unchanged for properties that do not qualify.”
To calculate the credit Ohio Department of Taxation created a one-time, mid-cycle adjustment to tax rates. Once the County received updated tax rates from the state, the software used to prepare and print bills had to be reprogrammed by the County Auditor’s Data Processing Department. Data Processing has sent the data to the third party vendor that prepares, prints and sends out bills and we expect tax bills to begin mailing in the next few days.
Please review this website and refer to the back of your bill for information including various methods of payment. Any questions you may call our office at 330-740-2460 or email mahoningcountytreasurer@mahoningcountyoh.gov .
Please be aware that postmarks may not necessarily reflect the date payments are dropped in the mail, nor do we have any control over the time it takes for the tax bill to be delivered once it is mailed. Taxpayers are encouraged to consider paying electronically, allow additional time for mailed payments, or request an in-person, hand-stamped postmark at the Post Office .
The office of the Treasurer of Mahoning County shall be open to full access by all members of the public . Our office hours are Monday through Friday 8 AM to 4:30 PM.
We encourage taxpayers to take advantage of our various electronic and online payment solutions which helps to accomplish accurate, efficient, and prompt recording of your payments. Please select Property Tax Payment Options on this website, instructions can also be found on the back of your tax bill.
NOTE: It is the taxpayer's responsibility to secure a tax bill. Failure to receive a tax bill will not void the 10% penalty for late payment.
